summary: The session discusses Toyota's approach to data governance and AI implementation, emphasizing the importance of a robust data architecture and the role of data ownership within business domains. Terry Martin outlines the challenges faced in managing data silos and the transition to a centralized data platform that enhances data accessibility and quality. The presentation highlights the integration of data products and governance frameworks to support AI readiness and operational efficiency.

sections.topic: Introduction and Overview of Toyota's Data Landscape
key_points: Toyota operates in a complex environment with extensive data generation across its European operations.
The data and AI team is structured into four teams focusing on governance, product delivery, AI innovation, and engineering.
Data silos lead to duplication and governance issues, complicating access to reliable data.
Power BI has become a non-governed data warehouse, resulting in quality and trust issues.
The strategy emphasizes 'Privacy by Design' and a single ingestion of data to avoid duplication.
Role-based access control is implemented to enhance data governance.
The data mesh concept allows business units to own their data domains and products.
A centralized data marketplace facilitates access to data products for all employees.
Data quality is monitored continuously to prevent defects from reaching consumers.
The 5S methodology is applied to maintain data organization and quality.
Plans to scale AI readiness and connect all agents on a unified governance backbone.
Emphasis on human oversight in AI and data management processes.

key_takeaways: Establish a centralized data governance framework to enhance data quality and accessibility.
Encourage business ownership of data domains to foster accountability and effective data management.
Implement continuous monitoring of data quality to prevent issues from affecting operational processes.
